findings.text: The positive-control claim asserts `bool(record_seed["within_factor_three"]) and 1.0/3.0 <= factor <= 3.0`, but `within_factor_three` was written by scripts/prototypes/stored_state_refusals/attribute_input_drift.py:235 as exactly `1.0/3.0 <= factor <= 3.0` over the same `factor` field read at verify_input_drift.py:102, so the first conjunct is the second and the claim cannot fail if the recorded residual constant at attribute_input_drift.py:64 is wrong; the verifier recomputes neither the residual nor the ratio, so the positive control's factor-of-three is not independently checked.

The arm log header is written on one line as `# arm=<label> revision=<sha> tree=<path> command: <cmd>`, but scripts/prototypes/stored_state_refusals/records.py:171-175 requires line one to start `# revision ` and line two `# command: `; running records.suite_arm_log on input-drift/suite-base.log raises `ValueError: first line is not '# revision <sha>'`, so the manifest's baseline_suite and after_suite log_path cannot be read back through the reader the same prototype package owns.

The exported arm trees are created with tempfile.mkdtemp(..., dir="/tmp") and the child environment sets TMPDIR=/tmp, which is a bare /tmp path rather than $TMPDIR; the dispatch and repo rule both say a temporary tree goes under $TMPDIR so it dies with the run's scratch, and the job log shows tree=/tmp/suite-arms-gloomfxa/base. non-blocking because the tree is removed in a finally block, but it is the rule the node was given.

`draw` re-implements the per-arm panel capability that scripts/prototypes/stored_state_refusals/redraw_panels.py:56-114 already owns: it draws one panel per arm terminal state through panels.draw_panel and writes the caption with panels.write_description/redraw_panels.py:56-114 already draws one panel per arm terminal state through panels.draw_panel and writes the caption with panels.write_description; the new driver copies that loop with a hard-coded ARMS table rather than extending redraw_panels.py to load a pickle when no npz terminal_flux exists, so the two drift apart on any change to panels.draw_panel's contract.

`_run_arm` re-implements the arm-runner and log-writer that scripts/prototypes/stored_state_refusals/run_suite_arm.sh:1-45 already owns (shared interpreter, PYTHONPATH=tree, JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu, '# revision' and '# command:' header, EXIT trailer); the addition does not extend that wrapper and instead forks the log format the package's reader rejects (see the finding at suite_arms.py:52), so which of the two writers a future arm uses decides whether its log can be read back.

PUBLISHED points at docs/figures/forward-solve-near-stored-states/stored-state-refusals, not docs/figures/forward-solve-near-stored-states/default-policy-refusal-drift, so test_published_panels_draw_both_series and test_published_previews_draw_the_blue_series never see the six SVGs this node published; a regression in drift_policy_panels.py that dropped a series would leave the suite green.

The seed-sensitivity table's nominal run reports residual 0.0042525413742888945 while the same nominal conditions at line 101 and the tcv-input-comparison panel caption report 0.004253522137685281, a 2.3e-4 relative scatter that the record does not remark; this is the prior review's finding f4d5e6f7a04 carried forward and still open, and the gained commits edited this table without addressing it.

The tests line records the gate as a prose sentence carrying `PYTHONPATH=<tree>` and a `-> 16 passed, EXIT=0` result rather than the literal command a shell was handed, so promotion, which fills its gate receipt from this line, cannot re-run either arm; the baseline_suite and after_suite blocks at manifest.md:14-15 carry a literal command but not the exported tree the arm ran in.
